lyrics:
[Intro: bright horn riff, clean guitar chops, rolling bass]

[Verse 1: smooth tenor, light and happy]
It was the second Friday in October
Streetlights humming, summer almost over
Your cousin's car, the radio on low
We didn't have a single place to go

[Pre-Chorus: falsetto joins, horns climb]
And the whole town smelled like rain and somebody's fire
Our hearts were ringing like a telephone wire

[Chorus: group vocals, falsetto on top, horns answering]
Sha-da-dee, say you were there
Sha-da-dee, leaves in your hair
Sha-da-dee, nothing went wrong
On the second Friday, all night long

[Verse 2: smooth tenor, bass busier]
Now the calendar has turned a few more pages
We've been all kinds of people, all kinds of ages
But when the air gets cool and the light gets gold
I am twenty-one and I'm not getting old

[Pre-Chorus: falsetto joins, horns climb]
And the whole town smells like rain and somebody's fire
My heart is ringing like a telephone wire

[Chorus: group vocals, falsetto on top, horns answering]
Sha-da-dee, say you were there
Sha-da-dee, leaves in your hair
Sha-da-dee, nothing went wrong
On the second Friday, all night long

[Horn Break: horn section trades with a kalimba, percussion]

[Bridge: falsetto lead, group answering]
Sha-da-dee-ya, dee-ya
(Was it the ninth? Was it the tenth?)
Sha-da-dee-ya, dee-ya
(Nobody knows, nobody cares)

[Final Chorus: everyone, horns wide open, falsetto ad-libs]
Sha-da-dee, say you were there
Sha-da-dee, leaves in your hair
Sha-da-dee, nothing went wrong
On the second Friday, all night long
Sha-da-dee, sha-da-dee
All night long

[Outro: horn riff, falsetto fading]
Sha-da-dee
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 126 BPM, 4/4, A major. A rolling, buoyant groove that never lets up. Pure celebration.

VOICE: A smooth male tenor carries the verses. A second man sings a pure, very high falsetto over the pre-chorus and choruses. A group of men sings the nonsense syllables in tight harmony. Falsetto ad-libs at the end.

INSTRUMENTS: A horn section (trumpets, trombones, saxophones) playing a bright, tight riff and answering the vocals. A clean electric guitar playing constant choppy chords. A busy, melodic electric bass. A crisp drum kit with a lively hi-hat. Congas and a cowbell. An African thumb piano (kalimba) in the break. Electric piano and strings.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, horn riff over guitar and bass. 0:15 Verse 1. 0:30 Pre-chorus. 0:45 Chorus 1. 1:00 Verse 2. 1:15 Pre-chorus. 1:30 Chorus 2. 1:45 Horn break with kalimba. 2:08 Bridge, falsetto and answering voices. 2:38 Final chorus, extended. 3:15 Outro, horns and fading falsetto to 3:35.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-1970s polished funk and soul: bright, clean and punchy, horns crisp, bass round, vocals stacked and smooth.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first 'sha-da-dee' at 0:45, with the falsetto above it.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: Verse 2 looks back from decades later and says the cool air still does it. The bridge admits nobody remembers the actual date, which is how real memories of perfect nights behave.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Joy remembered, joy relived.
